solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, answers clash); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Reports from family groups restraining Government

indicators.note: the family groups hold the government letter in check, so it sits inside them

parts.note: clans are family groups, especially in Scotland

explanation.surface: Accounts come in from family factions who are keeping the government in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Clangs are loud ringing noises, and a report can be a loud bang, so the plural nouns match.

clue.text: Starts to offer unkind criticism (harsh) that hurts

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters, taken in turn

explanation.surface: Unkind, harsh criticism is offered and it stings.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is what someone cries out when they feel pain, so it stands for the phrase as a whole.

clue.text: Businessman making money on the Italian ship

parts.note: il is Italian for the
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A tycoon earns his fortune from an Italian vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A milliner makes and sells hats, so is one kind of trader or businessman.

clue.text: Make money from tea producer by sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase says the word for the tea producer is to be heard rather than written

parts.note: an urn is a large vessel in which tea is made

explanation.surface: Someone profits from a tea-growing business, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent URN and EARN sound alike. 'Tea producer' looks like a plantation but is the urn.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to gain money through work, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Some have doubts about divine being

indicators.note: about here signals the run of letters is turned round
some of the words have doubts supplies a run of their letters

explanation.surface: Some people question the existence of a god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes AVED from 'have doubts'; 'about' turns it round to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A deva is a god or benign spirit in Hindu and Buddhist belief.

clue.text: Close to quay, needing hand tool for boat

indicators.note: the close of the word quay is its final letter

parts.note: an awl is a small pointed tool for piercing holes

explanation.surface: Near the quayside, someone needs a hand tool to work on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawl is a two-masted sailing vessel, one particular type of boat.

clue.text: Trip where a cult inhale, sadly?

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is this a drug trip, with the cult members unfortunately breathing something in?
explanation.definitionFit: To trip in slang is to have drug-induced visions, which is to see things that are not there.

clue.text: Ladies' clothing in Hello and Punch

parts.note: hi is an informal hello
a jab is a quick punch

explanation.surface: Women's fashion is featured in two magazines, Hello and Punch.
explanation.walkthrough: Hello and Punch look like British magazine titles, a celebrity weekly and a former humour magazine, but here they are plain words.
explanation.definitionFit: A hijab is a head covering worn by many Muslim women, an item of women's dress.

clue.text: Dry attitude

definitions.meaning: to dry washing is to hang it out in the breeze
a manner or bearing, as in an arrogant way about someone

explanation.surface: A wry, deadpan manner.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the verb for exposing laundry to the open, the other the noun for someone's manner.

clue.text: How the acre may be converted? Instruct once again

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A query on converting land measurements, then a request to explain it again.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix re- means again, so the word is to teach a second time, a synonym of instruct anew.

clue.text: Book hotel after girl not available

indicators.note: after places the hotel letter following the girl and the abbreviation

parts.note: Jo is a common girl's name
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A traveller tries to book a hotel but finds the girl unavailable.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonah is a book of the Old Testament, named for the prophet swallowed by a great fish.

clue.text: Lean adult adapted old carriage

indicators.note: adapted means altered to suit, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thin grown-up has been fitted into an antique coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A landaulet is a small landau, a horse-drawn coach with a folding hood, now a period vehicle.

clue.text: New front put on window frame in lower storey

indicators.note: the first letter of the window frame is exchanged for a different one

parts.note: a casement is a hinged window, or its frame

explanation.surface: Renovators fit a new front window frame on the lower floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not name the new letter; the definition shows the C becomes B.
explanation.definitionFit: A basement is the floor of a building partly or wholly below ground level.

clue.text: Pleasing sound character from Athens reproduced accurately

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
sic is written after a quotation to show it is copied exactly as found

explanation.surface: A Greek actor faithfully recreates a lovely sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' looks like a person in a play; it is a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Music is organised sound that is pleasant to listen to.

clue.text: Transported by lover, on about Italian city

indicators.note: the letters are carried within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Swept away by a lover going on about an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Verona is the setting of Romeo and Juliet.
explanation.definitionFit: Verona is a city in north-east Italy in the Veneto region.

clue.text: Seventies' contest

indicators.note: the possessive apostrophe stands for has, so the word Seventies has the letters within it

explanation.surface: A competition from the 1970s.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive apostrophe reads as 'has': the word Seventies has the answer inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is one competition within a sports meeting.

clue.text: At a distance from France

parts.note: of can mean from, as in a woman of Paris
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: Far away from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Off means away or removed, as in a town two miles off.

clue.text: Town House?

definitions.meaning: a Berkshire town west of London, home to the royal castle
the family name of the British royal dynasty since 1917

explanation.surface: A town house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Town house' reads as one phrase, a home in a city; split, the words are two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a Berkshire town with a castle, and the name of the reigning royal house.

clue.text: Vet English law changes: minor movement detected

indicators.note: changes means the letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: A vet notices a small shift as English law is altered.
explanation.definitionFit: A wavelet is a small wave, a slight motion of water.

clue.text: Knight with posh name, member of order

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
U stands for upper-class, a usage made famous by Nancy Mitford

explanation.surface: A titled knight with a smart name joins an order of chivalry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' suggests an order of knighthood; it is a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun belongs to a religious order of women living under vows.

clue.text: Indicating position as some might, flew Tornado from East

indicators.note: in an across entry, reading from the east means reading right to left, so the run is turned round
some of the words that follow supplies a run of their letters

explanation.surface: Pointing out their location, as some pilots might after flying a Tornado jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes HTFLEWT from the end of 'might', 'flew' and the T of 'Tornado'; 'from East' turns it round. The Tornado is an RAF jet.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelfth is an ordinal number, a word that states where something comes in a sequence.

clue.text: Dramatic scenes as expert (top class) is forced into short jacket

indicators.note: the expert and top-class pieces are squeezed inside the jacket

parts.note: tux is short for tuxedo, a dinner jacket
able means skilled or expert
A is the top grade or class

explanation.surface: Theatrical moments as a skilled first-rate performer is squeezed into a dinner jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Tableaux are scenes posed silently by actors, as in tableaux vivants, or striking dramatic moments.

clue.text: Bad habit, imbibing eye-opener before noon — port?

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the vice takes the other letters inside

parts.note: a vice is a bad habit

indicators.note: before puts the eye letter ahead of the noon letter

parts.note: the opener of the word eye is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bad habit: drinking an eye-opener before midday, port maybe?
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink being imbibed; it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice is a major Adriatic seaport in north-east Italy.

clue.text: Take away American bishop's pamphlet

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, and the possessive is read as is, giving S
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political

explanation.surface: Confiscate the leaflet an American bishop has been handing out.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract is to remove or extract something, a formal synonym for removing.

clue.text: Selfish desire to be seen with ace? That's right

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for an ace in cards
greed is selfish craving for more than one needs

explanation.surface: Is selfishness on show alongside a star player? Quite so.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying agreed is giving assent, the same as saying someone is correct.

clue.text: Pull: appeal (namely)

parts.note: to tow is to pull a vehicle along
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A pull, an appeal: that is to say, attraction defined.
explanation.definitionFit: To wit is an old legal phrase meaning that is to say.

clue.text: Lose time moving having to carry new building material

indicators.note: the rearranged letters bear the new letter within them
moving means the letters shift into new places

explanation.surface: Builders lose time shifting a new load of stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges LOSETIME into LIMESTOE; 'to carry' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Limestone is a sedimentary rock widely quarried for building and for making cement.

clue.text: After short time kiss flirt

indicators.note: after puts the kiss letter following the short time

parts.note: min is short for minute
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: After a brief moment comes a kiss: a flirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A minx is a cheeky, flirtatious young woman.

clue.text: Son is able to analyse verse

parts.note: can means is able to

explanation.surface: A son has a talent for studying poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan a line of poetry is to work out its metrical pattern.

clue.text: Just losing pounds? That's wrong — a stone!

indicators.note: losing tells us to remove the pounds letter from the word

parts.note: only means just, as in just one
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra
a cross, X, marks an answer as wrong

explanation.surface: A dieter has merely lost a few pounds? No, a whole stone!
explanation.walkthrough: 'stone' plays on the British weight of 14 pounds; it is a gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony, a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Keep quiet about wife, she's bad-tempered

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Say nothing about the wife: she's in a foul mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrew is a scolding, ill-tempered woman, as in The Taming of the Shrew.

clue.text: 25% of pack meet requirements

definitions.meaning: a pack of cards has four sets of thirteen, so one set is a quarter
to fit or be convenient for, as in that time works for me

explanation.surface: A quarter of the package satisfies the specification.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts, clubs, diamonds and spades are each a quarter of a deck; and to fit someone's needs is the verb sense.

clue.text: Head wheels cask

indicators.note: to wheel round is to turn about, so the word is turned back to front

parts.note: nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: The boss trundles a barrel along.
explanation.definitionFit: A tun is a large barrel for wine or beer.

clue.text: Bespoke work

definitions.meaning: made to the customer's own specification
a play by Shakespeare, a literary work

explanation.surface: Custom-made craftsmanship.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailored item is made to the client's wishes, and the phrase is also the title of a Shakespeare comedy.
